title: How Can Color Determine the Copper Content of Brass?
description: Chemistry Brass Colorimetry: use teacher-controlled brass digestion, quantitative dilution, a five-standard spectrophotometric calibration at an approved wavelength, and an independent color-depth comparison; keep the accepted teacher-configured per-wavelength distilled-water scan separate from the source-selected-wavelength calibration while determining copper mass percent.
audience: Chemistry students preparing for or documenting a supervised wet-lab investigation
learningGoals: Select and justify a Cu2+ analysis wavelength from 400-700 nm spectra while balancing sensitivity and working range.

Prepare quantitative transfers and a five-standard dilution series, then calibrate and use a spectrophotometer with defensible cuvette technique; keep the selected-wavelength calibration separate from teacher-configured per-wavelength scan settings.
Determine copper mass percent by regression and by matched color depth, compare precision and probable accuracy, and preserve safety evidence.
safetyNotes: Concentrated 15.8 M nitric acid addition, watch-glass covering, digestion, and the initial 50 mL water addition remain locked teacher actions inside an operating fume hood.
Wear splash-proof goggles, chemical-resistant gloves, and a protective apron. Keep nitric acid away from skin and incompatible materials.
NO rapidly forms toxic reddish-brown NO2 in air; the digestion must never unlock outside the hood.
Neutralize brass waste by adding baking soda in small portions until bubbling subsides and pH is 5-9, then follow the teacher-configured local disposal route.

feedback.success: Verify the five calibration pairs evidence accepted.

nodes.title: Submit the calibration slope

feedback.success: Submit the calibration slope evidence accepted.
